purpose: Archives the S3 packaging/runtime spike, its local evidence boundary and proposed multi-registry release design.
behavior: Explores npm platform optional packages without install scripts, abi3 Python wheels without source fallback and deferred-promise bridges sharing the core runtime.
Records a calibrated host-runtime SIGCHLD experiment: Linux fallback-reaper hangs under Node/Bun, distinct from the working pidfd path and dedicated wait mitigation.
Proposes native-target install matrices, registry-specific trusted publishing and versioned build tooling, with detailed reproduction/evidence ledger.
contracts: Banner explicitly says hosted CI never ran because billing blocked jobs; local ARM coverage is emulated and partial.
Q8 results concern processkit/tokio spike paths, not the current supervisor implementation.
failures_or_limits: Five-target/generated-loader/Python/OIDC release proposals are historical; current eight-target handwritten loader and read-only release workflow must be inspected independently.

> **EVIDENCE STATUS — read first.** The GitHub Actions run could not execute: every job of every run is
> refused with *"The job was not started because your account is locked due to a billing issue."*
> (org `HuGR-Labs`, free plan, public repo; runs
> [36939509378](https://github.com/HuGR-Labs/hugr-omni/actions/runs/36939509378),
> [36943725882](https://github.com/HuGR-Labs/hugr-omni/actions/runs/36943725882),
> [36946492376](https://github.com/HuGR-Labs/hugr-omni/actions/runs/36946492376); a rerun is refused the same way).
> That is an account/billing state only the Owner can fix; it is not a workflow defect. Therefore:
>
> * every answer below is backed by **LOCAL evidence** produced with the *same* scripts the workflow runs
>   (`spikes/packaging/ci/*.sh`), raw lines in `spikes/packaging/evidence/local-results.txt`;
> * local coverage = **darwin-x64** (native, macOS 15.3.2 Intel), **linux-x64-gnu** (Docker Desktop amd64, run earlier in the
>   session; Docker is now down and the disk nearly full, so nothing further could be added there) and **linux-arm64-gnu**
>   (Docker Desktop **emulated** with QEMU, *partial*: Node 22 install + smoke + Q7 only; Q8 never ran on arm64);
> * **Deno** was available only transiently (a global `npm` install of Deno 2.9.x, removed afterwards): its darwin-x64 and
>   linux-x64 results are real and kept, but cannot be re-run on this machine now; **Node 24 on macOS** likewise used a
>   temporary npm-installed binary (24.21.0);
> * **NOT VERIFIED anywhere: win32-x64-msvc and darwin-arm64** (no local machine; CI blocked), and **every GitHub-hosted
>   runner label (Q3) is documented but not exercised**;

### Q4 — Async runtime: one tokio runtime per process, owned by the core

**Answer / recommendation.** The core owns **one** lazily-initialised multi-thread tokio runtime
(`static RT: OnceLock<Runtime>`; built on the first async call, never at module load — `runtime_started()` is `false`
after `require`/`import` in every runtime and language). Bindings do not build runtimes; they hand a future to the
core and only *settle* a promise:

* **napi-rs:** do **not** use `#[napi] async fn` for product code. Stock napi (`tokio_rt`) starts its **own** runtime
  (threads named `tokio-rt-worker` in the harness, a second runtime next to ours). Use `Env::create_deferred()` →
  `JsDeferred`, spawn the work on the core runtime, and call `deferred.resolve/reject` from the tokio thread. napi
  creates the deferred together with a Node-API **threadsafe function** on the JS thread
  (`napi_create_threadsafe_function`), registers an env-cleanup hook, and `resolve()` ends in
  `napi_call_threadsafe_function`, so the JS value is created and the promise settled **on the JS thread**; if the env is
  tearing down, the pending deferred is rejected instead of touching a dead env (napi 3.14 `js_values/deferred.rs`).
  napi 3.14 also has an `async-runtime` SPI (`unsafe trait AsyncRuntime`, `register_async_runtime`): rejected, it is
  `unsafe`, brand new, and its contract (no thread may touch addon code after `shutdown`) is exactly the hard part.
* **PyO3:** `pyo3_async_runtimes::tokio::init_with_runtime(core::runtime())` (takes `&'static Runtime`, hence the
  `OnceLock`), then `future_into_py`. The future runs on the core runtime; on completion it takes the GIL on the tokio
  thread and completes the asyncio future through `loop.call_soon_threadsafe` (`pyo3-async-runtimes/src/generic.rs`,
  `call_soon_threadsafe`), so the event loop thread, not the tokio thread, resumes the awaiting coroutine.
  Cancelling the awaiting task is safe (the orphaned tokio task finishes into a cancelled future).

**Finding 1 — the exposure depends on how tokio waits, not only on the runtime.** tokio 1.53 has two child reapers
(`src/process/unix/mod.rs: build_child`): `PidfdReaper` on Linux when `pidfd_open` succeeds (kernel ≥ 5.3 and not blocked by
seccomp), otherwise `SignalReaper`, which is woken only by tokio's own SIGCHLD handler (macOS/BSD, and Linux without
pidfd: older kernels — check distro backports, e.g. RHEL 8 ships a 4.18-based kernel — or sandboxes that block `pidfd_open`). On the pidfd path SIGCHLD is irrelevant: the
sabotage control cannot hang it (`control … detected=no note=linux-pidfd-path-does-not-use-SIGCHLD`) and the real
scenarios show 0 hangs. To exercise the other path on Linux a second container pass runs with a seccomp profile that
returns `ENOSYS` for `pidfd_open` (`ci/seccomp-no-pidfd.json`); there the control is detected.

**Finding 2 — measured hang counts** (processkit waits hung / total; native waits never hung):
| runtime (native spawn API tested) | macOS darwin-x64 (SIGCHLD-driven reaper) | Linux x64, kernel-default (pidfd reaper) | Linux x64, **SIGCHLD reaper** (pidfd blocked by seccomp) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Node 22.17 / 22.23 (`child_process`) | 0 hangs — a, b, c × 50 it | 0 hangs — a, b, c × 50 it | **HANG a** (3/4 pk waits hung, breaker at it 2) · **HANG b** (3/4, it 4) · **HANG c** (5/6, it 3) |
| Node 24.21 (`child_process`) | 0 | 0 | **HANG a** (5/8, it 4) · **HANG b** (3/4, it 4) · **HANG c** (17/28, it 14) |
| Bun 1.3.14 (`Bun.spawn` and `node:child_process`) | 0 | 0 | **HANG a** (3/4, it 2) · b: 0 hangs (50/50 it) · **HANG c** (3/4, it 2) |
| Deno 2.9.x (`Deno.Command` and `node:child_process`) | 0 | 0 | 0 hangs in a, b, c |
| *std::process + blocking wait (mitigation)*, all four runtimes | 0 | 0 | 0 (50 it × a, b, c each) |
| Windows | no SIGCHLD — not applicable, not run | | |

**Finding 3 — mitigation that works (experiment, not processkit):** run the child with `std::process` and wait for it on
a dedicated blocking thread (`spawn_blocking(child.wait)`, i.e. `waitpid` on that one pid; `runCommandStd` in the addon).
It never depends on SIGCHLD or on tokio's signal driver: 0 hangs in every scenario and runtime on the signal path
(`pk_impl=stdwait … verdict=NO_HANG`), and it survives the sabotage control on the two runtimes where that second control ran
(`RESULT Q8 mitigation-survives-sabotage target=darwin-x64 rt=node22|bun … yes`; NOT RUN on Linux, Node 24, Deno).

**Reading for the pivot (judgement, flagged as such).** processkit on the **pidfd path** coexists with libuv/Bun/Deno in
every combination tried. On the **signal path** it does not under **Node 22, Node 24 and Bun** (Linux; Deno never hung). macOS shows 0 hangs for all four
runtimes, but macOS is a SIGCHLD-driven platform, so that result rests on libuv/Bun/Deno *not* clobbering tokio's handler
there (observed: `sigchldState()` stays `handler` across native spawns) — a property of today's runtime versions, not a guarantee. Because the glibc floor chosen in Q1 (2.17) deliberately
admits CentOS/RHEL 7–8 era kernels, **a design that waits through tokio's SIGCHLD reaper is not safe inside the three
host runtimes on every supported Linux**. Either wait via per-child blocking `waitpid` in the core (shown to work), or
adopt processkit only after it offers a wait path independent of SIGCHLD (and re-run this harness as a gate).

1. **npm:** root package + 5 optional platform packages, built with `@napi-rs/cli` 3.x / napi 3.x, `napi8`, Linux glibc
   targets cross-built with `--use-napi-cross` (glibc ≥ 2.17), CJS loader generated by the CLI, **no lifecycle
   scripts, ever**; `engines.node >=22`. Per-package publish with trusted publishing; do **not** use `napi pre-publish`
   (it runs `npm publish`); keep `optionalDependencies` static and assert them in CI (`check-tarballs.mjs`).
2. **PyPI:** maturin 1.15 + PyO3 0.29, `abi3-py310`, mixed layout (`python-source`), wheels only — **no sdist is uploaded
   to PyPI** (an sdist makes `pip` fall back to compiling on an unsupported platform; we want "No matching distribution"
   instead). manylinux_2_28 on x64 and on the native arm runner, `macosx_10_12_x86_64` / `macosx_11_0_arm64`, `win_amd64`.
   `pip install --only-binary=:all:` and uv are both release gates.
3. **crates.io:** plain source crates; keep `cc`-based build scripts out of the dependency graph so the only native
   requirement of a Rust consumer is the linker rustc already needs.
4. **Runtime:** one lazily-built tokio runtime owned by the core; bindings only settle promises/futures
   (napi `JsDeferred`; PyO3 `pyo3-async-runtimes` + `init_with_runtime`). No `#[napi] async fn`, no napi `async-runtime`
   SPI, no PyO3 `experimental-async` in product code.
5. **Runners:** `ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `windows-latest`, `macos-latest` (arm64), `macos-15-intel` — documented,
   pending a first successful run.
6. **Install tests:** fresh job per (target × runtime/installer), installing the packed artefacts from a localhost registry
   fixture through the runtime's own package manager; Linux in slim, compiler-free containers; Deno with
   `--allow-ffi --allow-env --allow-read` (Linux; macOS needs no read).
7. **Release:** a single `release.yml`, three environment-gated jobs, trusted publishing on all three registries, no
   long-lived tokens after the one-time manual first publishes (Q5).
8. **Process waiting (Q7/Q8):** do not let the product's correctness depend on tokio's SIGCHLD-driven reaper while hosted
   inside Node/Bun/Deno. processkit is acceptable only behind a gate: the Q8 harness (including its positive control and
   the pidfd-blocked pass) must be green on every target before any adoption, or the core waits with dedicated blocking
   `waitpid` threads. **This is the lead's decision; the ADR records the evidence and the cheaper safe option.**

purpose: Preserves independent static rejections of the S1/S2 proposals and the reasoning that led to ADR-0005.
behavior: Separates supported Windows containment/no-signal-hook principles from unproved host-side watchdog ownership, identity pinning and console mutation.
Identifies atomic spawn ownership, checked initialization, bounded channels, full descriptor hygiene and independent unknown-liveness handling as product requirements.
Challenges PTY close deadlines, unbounded pumps, thread-unsafe ptsname, normalizers hiding changes and green workflows that only print counters.
contracts: Review explicitly did not independently retrieve hosted logs or rerun the full spikes.
Reject is a historical review verdict; proposals are corrective requirements rather than findings against every current baseline module.
failures_or_limits: Mechanism benchmarks and N/N logs cannot prove a complete product contract.
Normalizer counterexamples and missing failure propagation narrow the cited spike evidence, not current conformance results.
gaps: Current implementation closure of each historical finding requires source-specific evidence elsewhere.

evidence.quote:
Independent, read-only reviews by Codex CLI of the spike ADRs and the spike code that produced their evidence
(2026-10-02). Both returned `reject` as a product baseline; the lead's response is ADR-0005 (supervisor).

## ADR-0001 + ADR-0002 (process model, host exit)

**Verdict:** `reject` — Neither ADR is safe to adopt unchanged as a product baseline. Windows jobs and avoiding native signal chaining are well supported. Unix supervision needs checked initialization, atomic spawn ownership, and identity safety that survives foreign reapers and host death; an exec'd supervisor is the safer foundation. Windows console attachment must leave the embedding host untouched. Review covered source and platform documentation; quoted CI logs could not be independently retrieved, and no files were modified.

| must_fix | Post-fork safety requires a complete argument; prefer an exec'd helper | ADR-0002:166 treats 'only async-signal-safe calls' as established. After fork from a multithreaded host, locks and allocator state can belong to vanished threads; every reachable operation must remain safe until exec, including inherited signal handlers. The fixed arrays avoid obvious heap allocation, but watchdog.rs does not reset inherited handlers/masks and provides no platform audit of Darwin kqueue/kevent or the Rust/libc call paths. nanosleep lacks a portable POSIX async-safety guarantee, although glibc documents its implementation as AS-safe. Successful minimal-host runs cannot prove absence of rare deadlocks. Fork without exec is not categorically forbidden, but this implementation has not established its required conditions. [POSIX fork requirements](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/009695399/functions/fork.html), [signal-safety list](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/signal-safety.7.html), [glibc nanosleep safety](https://sourceware.org/glibc/manual/2.42/html_node/Sleeping.html) | Ship a small versioned helper and start it through posix_spawn where supported, with explicit signal defaults/mask and descriptor actions. Exec gives the helper fresh runtime and allocator state. If retaining no-exec operation, require a platform-specific audit of its complete call graph, signal sanitization, startup races, and error paths; allocation/lock contention tests supplement that audit. |
| must_fix | Hostile reapers defeat the advertised Unix identity guarantee | ADR-0001:259 promises zombie pinning while ADR-0001:315 supports SIGCHLD=SIG_IGN and foreign waitpid(-1). Explicit SIG_IGN, SA_NOCLDWAIT, or a competing reaper can remove the zombie regardless of WNOWAIT. A pidfd identifies its original process but does not preserve a zombie or make a later numeric killpg safe; kqueue is also an observer. A SIGCHLD handler that waits only for its own children is compatible, whereas a catch-all reaper is not. [pidfd_open prerequisites](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html) | Either require exclusive child-reaping ownership and explicitly narrow supported-host guarantees, or make an independent helper the actual parent of managed roots, with its own SIGCHLD policy. Do not continue numeric group signaling after ownership is lost. Add tests combining foreign reaping, retained Child handles, group disappearance, and PID/PGID reuse. |
| must_fix | Zombie pinning ends at host death | The watchdog is the root's sibling, not its parent. When the host dies, retained zombies can be reparented and reaped. After watchdog SIGTERM, the group can disappear and its number become reusable before the delayed SIGKILL at watchdog.rs:142. An unrelated group could then receive SIGKILL. Untracking before normal reaping does not protect this host-death path. | Have the surviving supervisor own and retain root zombies through its final group signal, or use a verified stable containment identity. Exercise host death after root exit and group disappearance during grace, with an unrelated-process sentinel. Exec alone does not solve this ownership problem. |
| must_fix | Spawn-to-watchdog registration gap | ADR-0002:205 requires tracking after the group exists. Abrupt host death between posix_spawn and the track write leaves a running tree unknown to the watchdog. unix.rs:466 spawns before tracking, and all Q5/Q6 death tests wait until registration has completed. An acknowledgment after tracking alone cannot close the earlier gap. | Use a supervisor-owned spawn transaction, or another mechanism that prevents target execution before durable supervision is established. Inject host death at each startup boundary. Until then, describe cleanup as applying only to successfully registered trees. |
| must_fix | Watchdog liveness is insufficient; IPC and initialization are unchecked | watchdog.rs:26 does not handle fork failure; death-handle creation and registration errors are ignored. Track writes are blocking, unchecked writes despite the non-blocking contract. Full pipes can stall the host, failed writes lose supervision, and a broken pipe can invoke SIGPIPE behavior. The 256-entry table silently drops additional groups. Descriptor cleanup closes only descriptors below 1024, and mapping /dev/null onto standard descriptors can overwrite the pipe if it occupied descriptor 0, 1, or 2. A living but stopped, wedged, or improperly armed watchdog provides no cleanup. | Specify a checked startup handshake, explicit capacity/backpressure policy, protected IPC descriptors, complete descriptor cleanup, and failure behavior for every syscall. Define T2 in terms of a successfully armed, responsive supervisor. Test exhausted descriptors, failed process creation, denied pidfd/kqueue operations, full IPC, dead/stopped helpers, and more than 256 trees. |

| must_fix | Printed success counts are not acceptance gates | Q1, Q4, Q5, and much of Q7 print failed outcomes without failing the executable. The workflow merely collects RESULT lines; nightly steps additionally allow failure. Thus 'all green' does not establish the quoted architectural outcomes. Q1's late-assignment/preemption controls and Q5's no-mechanism controls are valuable, but Q7's ESRCH row does not exercise ID reuse, and no control validates escalation against a SIGTERM-resistant tree. | Assert each expected outcome and its counterexample, including intentionally failing controls, and make discrepancies fail CI. Add registration-race, forced-escalation, and identity-reuse scenarios. Preserve raw results with source SHA and platform versions; characterize 100/100 as observed trials rather than a proof of correctness. |
| must_fix | Several observation errors can be reported as success | unix.rs:922 counts every event-registration error as an observed exit. exit_watch_wait accepts any returned event without validating NOTE_EXIT, EV_ERROR, or poll event flags. The raw spawn benchmark ignores posix_spawnattr_setflags's result and never checks SID/PGID. On macOS, is_zombie at unix.rs:63 treats any proc_pidinfo failure plus successful kill(pid,0) as a zombie, potentially classifying a live but unobservable process as dead. | Separate verified exit, unavailable status, registration failure, and unknown liveness. Validate event identity/flags and all setup return values. Add delayed-live controls and injected observation failures; use a reliable secondary liveness oracle instead of equating inspection failure with death. |
| should_fix | Grace policy has no supporting experiment or protocol | ADR-0002:178 introduces max-live-tree grace and a five-second cap, while the spike stores one startup grace and transmits no per-tree grace. Its fixtures terminate on SIGTERM, so reported sub-millisecond cleanup does not exercise the delayed forced phase. nanosleep interruption is also ignored. | Identify this as an unvalidated policy choice, define how grace values reach the supervisor, and test mixed graces, untracking the maximum, capping, interrupted waits, and descendants that ignore SIGTERM. Use monotonic deadlines for escalation. |
| must_fix | GUARANTEES exceed their mechanisms | T1 correctly distinguishes kernel enforcement from T2, and Unix escape exclusions are useful. However, T2 currently requires more than a living watchdog: successful registration, responsiveness, valid group identity, and permission to signal all relevant members. Unix graceful delivery is best effort too. Group membership alone does not overcome changed credentials. Forced termination should not imply immediate resource reclamation or a strict exit deadline. Windows process groups also are not console isolation: children can re-enable Ctrl-C, and CTRL_BREAK reaches only group members sharing the sender's console. [Windows console semantics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/generateconsolectrlevent), [handler behavior](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/setconsolectrlhandler), [asynchronous termination](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-terminateprocess) | Separate containment scope, graceful delivery, forced-termination request, exit observation, and bounded completion. State each tier's prerequisites and failure/degradation behavior. Remove unconditional host-behavior and terminal-signal claims until the console design and supervisor ownership are fixed. |
| should_fix | Normal PTY job control exceeds one process group | ADR-0001:253 includes PTY children, but interactive shells normally create additional process groups for foreground/background jobs. Those jobs escape root killpg without malicious daemonization. The Q4 terminal test checks inherited-terminal reads, not an interactive shell running a pipeline or background job under the proposed PTY setup. | Exercise shell job control and scope/host cleanup of foreground and background jobs. Make the practical PTY limitation explicit or provide a stronger containment tier. Specify how the direct spawn path establishes the controlling terminal; TIOCSCTTY is not a standard spawn file action. |
| should_fix | Zombie and job-handle ownership need a product lifecycle contract | ADR-0001:327 acknowledges that retained Child handles retain zombie roots indefinitely. This consumes process-table resources and conflicts with hostile-host support. ADR-0002 ties job lifetime to Child lifetime while PLAN.md:155 forbids GC from killing live processes; binding finalization therefore cannot simply release the last job handle. | Define who owns containment and supervision independently of language-wrapper reachability, when signaling becomes permanently unavailable, and how explicit disposal, GC, completed-but-retained handles, and leaks affect resources. Bound zombie retention to a documented cleanup lifecycle and validate repeated completed commands. |
| should_fix | Benchmark and compatibility conclusions are broader than the experiment | Q8 compares a raw Unix spawn with empty environment, inherited stdio, and no file actions against std's inherited environment and null/piped stdio. It omits supervision, registration, reactors, and the product's full setup. The Windows variants also differ in setup. Q2 covers several outer-job flags but not documented nested-job restrictions such as UI limits. Bun/Deno and actual napi-rs/PyO3 integration remain untested. | Keep Q8 as a mechanism microbenchmark, not a demonstrated product K4 result. Compare equivalent argv/env/cwd/stdio and full lifecycle costs with interleaved measurements. Test nested-job failure cleanup and the intended embedding runtimes before extending product guarantees. [Nested-job restrictions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/nested-jobs) |

**Verdict:** `reject` — The spike supports atomic CLOEXEC opening, basic ConPTY pipe ownership, explicit standard handles, resizing and JOB_LIST containment. The ADR is unsafe to freeze because deadline enforcement, host-global Ctrl+C changes, Unix containment and output guarantees exceed the evidence. Source and read-only checker counterexamples were inspected; hosted run logs could not be independently retrieved, and the full spike was not rerun.

| must_fix | ConPTY close blocks enforcement of graceMs | ADR Q2's sketch calls ClosePseudoConsole and joins before its timeout branch. own_win.rs implements synchronous close, including in Drop. Before 26100, close waits for pseudoconsole exit, so a stubborn client can consume roughly five seconds even with a two-second grace, and an actual hang can prevent escalation indefinitely. A separate reader does not make the closer nonblocking. [Microsoft's close contract](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/closepseudoconsole) explicitly describes the older indefinite wait. | Run close on a dedicated worker while an independent supervisor enforces an absolute deadline measured from root exit. Define safe synchronization with write/resize, retain Job ownership through escalation, and join only after bounded teardown. Test close-first-then-deadline-kill with a stubborn writer on pre-26100 Windows, including graceMs below five seconds and a blocked close. |
| must_fix | Process-global Ctrl+C mutation | NULL/FALSE preserves registered handler functions but enables their delivery and potentially the default terminating handler. Leaving it cleared changes the host permanently; temporary toggling exposes a signal window and changes inheritance for concurrent unrelated children. A library-local spawn lock cannot serialize Node, Python or other native modules. The previous ignore state has no documented getter. [Microsoft documents these semantics](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/setconsolectrlhandler). | Remove host mutation from the default design. Spike a console-attached launcher or broker that clears its own flag before launching the target, with Job containment, target PID/exit reporting and spawn-error propagation. Alternatively require explicit host opt-in to a documented global policy. Verify host handlers and unrelated child inheritance with the host initially ignoring and processing Ctrl+C. |
| must_fix | Unix session sweep is not a whole-tree guarantee | ADR Decision 3 and INV-04 treat session membership as complete containment. An escaped session is explicitly acknowledged but left outside the decision. A single enumeration also races with forks, and numeric PID checks followed by kill can target a reused PID. jobctl checks survivors from the original snapshot, so newly created descendants would not invalidate its result. macOS EOF can occur while jobs remain alive. | Define the containment mechanism and process-identity lifetime before freezing kill_tree. Use stronger containment where available, or explicitly narrow the portable guarantee. Test setsid escape, forks during cleanup and survivors after EOF using fresh inventories. Do not infer tree death from EOF or claim that cancelling a reader kills escaped processes. |
| must_fix | Reader cancellation and output backpressure | Stream::spawn detaches a blocking reader with no cancellation or join handle. An escaped Unix slave holder can retain that thread and its master fd after the owner drops. The unbounded channel lets the spike drain independently of consumers; a bounded production queue could block draining and recreate the ConPTY close deadlock. EOF absence can also mean stalled rendering or draining, not just a stubborn descendant. | Specify cancellable readers and explicit worker ownership. On Unix, use nonblocking reads with a wake mechanism; define Windows cancellation and teardown separately. Specify buffering or spooling behavior when the JS consumer stalls. Exercise drop, cancellation, slow consumers and escaped slave holders while checking workers and descriptors return to baseline. |
| must_fix | Inherited Unix descriptors and spawning without pre_exec | Atomic PTY opening prevents PTY-specific leakage but does not remove the host's existing inheritable sockets, files or pipes. The observed non-tty descriptors demonstrate that gap. The proposed close_range/fcntl remedy exists only in pre_exec; applying it in the parent would mutate host descriptors. Conversely, closing descriptors through controlled spawn file actions does not inherently reproduce portable-pty's destruction of Rust's private exec-error pipe. | Choose an explicit spawning backend and fd allowlist. For pre_exec, mark unwanted descriptors CLOEXEC using async-signal-safe operations while preserving error reporting. Without pre_exec, use macOS POSIX_SPAWN_CLOEXEC_DEFAULT with explicit inheritance and Linux posix_spawn_file_actions_addclosefrom_np after required mappings, with supported-version fallbacks. Prove controlling-terminal setup separately; setsid plus dup2 is not a portable substitute for TIOCSCTTY. Use a launcher if required. [glibc's closefrom spawn action](https://sourceware.org/pipermail/glibc-cvs/2021q3/073654.html) provides a concrete alternative. |
| must_fix | Concurrent PTY creation through ptsname | own_unix.rs:64-68 obtains a pointer from ptsname() and then opens it. Another thread can overwrite its static storage between those operations, attaching a session to the wrong slave. The fd race experiment has one PTY-opening thread and cannot expose this. [Linux documents ptsname as MT-Unsafe](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/ptsname.3.html). | Use ptsname_r on supported Linux targets and a caller-buffer API such as TIOCPTYGNAME on macOS. [node-pty uses TIOCPTYGNAME specifically to avoid threading problems](https://github.com/microsoft/node-pty/blob/main/src/unix/pty.cc). Add concurrent PTY-session isolation evidence. |
| must_fix | Normalizer hides user-visible differences | stream.rs:105-161 discards CR, backspace, erase operations, cursor columns, styling, titles, hyperlinks and terminal modes; it also trims whitespace and invents a final newline. Its append-only collector cannot model overwriting, scrolling, wrapping or alternate screens. Distinct rendered output can pass, and equivalent rendering can fail. Making this the sole contract oracle weakens K5 silently. | Limit this matcher to named simple-text fixtures. Compare ordered text without trimming meaningful whitespace, verify raw transport preservation separately, and use a real terminal-state oracle for rendering behavior. Require controls showing that altered whitespace, final newlines, cursor operations and modes are detected by the appropriate oracle. |
| must_fix | Every-byte delivery and UTF-8 claims exceed the evidence | ADR line 290 promises every byte written by the child despite ConPTY being a renderer. The burst checker uses a HashSet and ignores ordering, duplication and extra output; read-only counterexamples pass with reversed or duplicated lines. The UTF-8 sample is normalized after complete accumulation, so it does not test chunk-boundary decoding in the binding. Stream also treats every non-interrupted read error as successful EOF. | Distinguish child writes, PTY transformations and bytes emitted by the PTY backend. Promise preservation of the defined output stream within explicit limits. Check ordered records, multiplicity and unexpected data; distinguish expected EOF errors from transport failures. Test partial UTF-8 sequences, final incomplete sequences, wrapping, overwrite and resize/reflow through the actual binding. |
| must_fix | Green CI is not an acceptance gate | ci.sh:3-13 uses neither errexit nor pipefail, prints PIPESTATUS without propagating it, and does not validate RESULT counters. Probes normally exit successfully even when they report failures. A watchdog exit, panic, missing experiment or bad N/N result can therefore coexist with a green job. | Propagate unexpected probe failures and validate experiment-specific outcomes, including expected failures in control modes. Require the complete result set and requested iteration counts, and fail on watchdogs, malformed output and unexpected counters. Retain complete logs as artifacts and describe current runs as observations rather than passing acceptance. |

purpose: Archives a source-only audit of processkit v3.3.4/ba1a6fe as an alternative dependency.
behavior: Credits suspended Windows Job assignment and conditional delegated-cgroup containment, while rejecting universal Unix no-orphans and abrupt-host-death claims.
Identifies Unix PTY CLOEXEC leakage, raw ConPTY input/batch validation, silence-driven EOF, delayed pumps and silent incomplete capture as adapter/upstream work.
Distinguishes meaningful real-process test sources from unexercised cgroup branches, then documents source size, rapid API churn and concentrated authorship.
contracts: Audit verdict is build_on_it_with_fixes at the named tag; nothing was built or executed.
Line counts include comments/inline tests, not an asserted production-statement count.
failures_or_limits: These are historical third-party audit findings, not claims about current processkit or Omni code.
Sampled unsafe paths did not establish definite UB; absence of such a finding is not an exhaustive safety proof.
gaps: Audit does not itself validate hosted test execution or fixes after the pinned version.

evidence.quote:
Static review of the source and tests at tag v3.3.4 (commit ba1a6fe) by Codex CLI, read-only, without
relying on the README. Nothing was built or executed here; the hands-on evaluation is `processkit-eval.md` (E1).

**Verdict:** `build_on_it_with_fixes`

The inspected source supports race-free Windows startup containment and conditional Linux cgroup containment, backed by meaningful real-process tests. A production TypeScript package needs PTY fd and input-validation fixes, bounded ConPTY drainage, explicit incomplete-capture reporting, bounded output handling, and honest containment/host-death capabilities. Universal cross-platform no-orphans guarantees do not hold. Assessment is static at ba1a6fe/v3.3.4; nothing was built or executed.

| 6. Unsafe code and signal/async safety | concerns | The sampled fork-to-exec hooks prepare allocations in the parent and use stack formatting and syscall-style operations in the child: cgroup join uses open/write/close (src/sys/linux.rs:2939), PDEATHSIG uses prctl/getppid/_exit (:2919), and terminal setup uses setsid/ioctl (src/sys/pty/unix.rs:469, :485). No allocator/lock call between fork and exec, definite UB, or double close was established in these sampled paths. Windows handle transfer clears the previous owner's handle before constructing File (src/sys/pty/windows.rs:1002), and detached waits retain process ownership through Arc (:224). However, Unix openpty descriptors are wrapped without setting FD_CLOEXEC (src/sys/pty/unix.rs:185, :198). The later fcntl changes only O_NONBLOCK (:214, :219), and the pre_exec hooks do not close the original master. On implementations returning inheritable openpty fds, the executed child and unrelated concurrent launches inherit unintended terminal descriptors. An exec-time fd inventory test would establish the precise platform impact. |
| 7. Error handling and public-path panics | concerns | Public-path implementations contain poisoned-mutex expects, including SharedLines and raw capture (src/pump.rs:686; src/running/mod.rs:1692), and ConPTY reader/writer state (src/sys/pty/windows.rs:1265, :1522). Several ownership expects appear protected by internal invariants; no ordinary-input violation of those invariants was established. Line-handler panics are caught and disable that handler (src/pump.rs:188); a panicking stdin source has a real error-propagation test (tests/integration/capture.rs:968). Actual pump read errors are recorded and surfaced (src/pump.rs:1815; src/running/mod.rs:2201). Pump task panics and drain timeouts are nevertheless swallowed as run errors (src/running/mod.rs:3798), tee write failures disable the tee, and tee flush errors are ignored (src/pump.rs:1454, :1493, :1802). Drop cleanup is best-effort and cannot report failure. Raw ConPTY launch also bypasses std's normal spawn-time input validation. |
| 8. Tests and platform proof | concerns | These are not merely mocks. Actual tree tests include windows_grandchild_is_contained (tests/integration/groups.rs:133), windows_nested_job_assign_and_kill_all (:950), windows_nested_job_outer_close_reaps_tree (:1020), unix_setsid_child_forks_grandchild_still_contained (:230), and unix_fork_storm_is_swept_by_group_broadcast (tests/integration/process_control.rs:134). The Unix setsid test covers a direct child intentionally starting a session; its grandchild does not independently escape. A real Linux setsid-escapee cgroup test exists (src/sys/linux.rs:6007), but returns successfully when delegation is unavailable (:5670, :6008). CI runs ignored tests on Linux, Windows, and macOS (.github/workflows/ci.yml:105, :130); no mandatory delegated-cgroup setup was found. pty_finish_sends_console_eof_without_closing_the_session proves ConPTY input EOF (tests/integration/pty.rs:454). concurrent_pty_sessions_stay_correct_at_scale checks output markers and completion (tests/stress/main.rs:422, :465), and is scheduled on all three OSes (.github/workflows/stress.yml:40). Neither distinguishes actual output EOF from the five-second pump-abort fallback; no test directly proves prompt ClosePseudoConsole output EOF, complete final-frame drainage, or PTY startup-grandchild containment. Windows abrupt-owner-death coverage is also absent from the Unix-gated parent-death suite (tests/integration/main.rs:28). No tests were executed during this audit. |
| 9. Maintainability, churn, and API stability | concerns | Measured src contains 86,342 lines across 58 Rust files; 28 exceed 650 lines. This includes substantial comments and inline tests, not 86k production statements. Large lifecycle modules include src/command.rs:101 (6,586 total lines), src/running/mod.rs:839 (6,403), src/sys/linux.rs:107 (6,331), and src/pump.rs:1414 (5,258). HEAD ba1a6fe identifies v3.3.4 (Cargo.toml:3). Its history contains 1,108 commits from 2026-05-31 through 2026-08-22, including 102 dated 2026-07-08. Major lines arrived rapidly: v1.0.0 on June 16 (73a812c), v2.1.0 on July 6 (66c8c66), and v3.0.0 on July 25 (c4c537c). Source-changing commits demonstrate genuine breakage: field/API renames (d7c5f61), alias removal (d19c631), Error boxing (a40dff9; current src/error.rs:1350), and OutputEvent-to-ProcessEvent rename (9cb59aa; current src/running/stream.rs:1023). Two author identities belonging to Anton account for 868 commits; another 201 use Test <test@test.com>. Bus factor is uncertain but visibly concentrated; those anonymous commits cannot establish independent maintainers. |

| P0 | `src/sys/linux.rs:118` | Whole-tree kill-on-drop provides an unconditional no-orphans guarantee. | Linux silently accepts process-group fallback without tracing when cgroup creation fails. Descendants that change process groups survive cleanup; macOS always has this boundary. A TypeScript API must expose the weaker capability or refuse launches requiring stronger containment. |
| P0 | `src/sys/linux.rs:2919` | Host termination reliably cleans up the process tree. | Default Unix SIGINT/SIGTERM, SIGKILL, abort, and process::exit bypass Drop. Optional Linux PDEATHSIG reaches only the direct child; the real test explicitly expects grandchildren to survive. macOS has no abrupt-death cleanup. Host signal handlers can improve graceful termination, but cannot supply universal SIGKILL cleanup. |
| P1 | `src/sys/pty/unix.rs:198` | Unix PTY descriptors remain confined to their intended owners. | The original openpty master and slave are never marked close-on-exec, and no pre_exec hook closes the master. Inheritable descriptors leak into executed children and potentially concurrent launches. Set close-on-exec before launch and verify inherited fd inventories on Linux and macOS. |
| P1 | `src/sys/pty/windows.rs:431` | ConPTY preserves the normal process-launch input validation boundary. | The raw environment builder copies embedded NULs and invalid names directly. For example, a value containing "ok\u0000INJECTED=yes" becomes two environment entries. Command-line construction likewise permits NUL truncation. Building a tokio Command does not perform the spawn-time validation because this path calls CreateProcessW directly. Reject invalid inputs before serialization and add Windows regression tests. |
| P1 | `src/sys/pty/windows.rs:124` | Waiting for the ConPTY child reaches output EOF promptly after that child exits. | Quiescence restarts indefinitely while output arrives. A surviving descendant that continually renders can keep wait pending after the direct child exits. Conversely, 100 ms of silence does not establish that every delayed final frame arrived. Add an overall drain bound and tests for both continuous descendant output and delayed final rendering. |
| P1 | `src/sys/pty/windows.rs:878` | PTY launch supports the same Windows executable and batch commands as ordinary launch. | Ordinary launch reaches std's batch handling; ConPTY directly submits a .bat/.cmd path to CreateProcessW with only MSVCRT argument quoting. There is no equivalent batch dispatch or hostile-argument test. Reject batch PTY launches explicitly or implement and test an appropriate safe launch path. |
| P1 | `src/running/mod.rs:3791` | Successful capture accurately reports whether output was completely drained. | Pump panics are ignored, and five-second drain timeouts abort pumps without returning a capture error. Text truncation is computed only from buffer-policy drops at line 1578. A successful result can therefore contain incomplete output with truncated=false; an unfinished text tail can also be lost. Report pump completion and preserve partial tails. |
| P1 | `src/running/mod.rs:867` | Starting a process protects an unattended caller from output blockage and uncontrolled memory growth. | Pumps are initially absent, so an unattended handle can leave OS pipes full. After pumps start, default capture grows without bound, and a line-count limit alone permits an arbitrarily large unfinished line. A TypeScript wrapper needs deliberate eager drainage, byte limits, and callback/tee backpressure semantics. |
| P1 | `src/sys/linux.rs:5677` | The platform test matrix establishes the strongest containment and ConPTY EOF claims. | Real cgroup tests can return success without exercising cgroups, and CI does not require delegation. Existing ConPTY completion tests can pass through pump-abort fallback. Require a delegated Linux test lane and a Windows output-EOF assertion that cannot pass after aborting the reader. |
| P2 | `src/command.rs:101` | The crate is a small, stable substrate with distributed maintenance ownership. | The source spans 86,342 lines, lifecycle responsibilities occupy several multi-thousand-line modules, and three major API lines appeared within weeks. Commit authorship is concentrated, with a substantial anonymous Test identity. Pin the Rust version and isolate its evolving API behind a narrow binding contract. |

purpose: Archives the independent static review of the S5 supervisor spike and conditions before a product freeze.
behavior: Accepts the architectural direction with changes, crediting resistant-tree stop assertions, exact PID-reuse controls and paired K4 methodology while narrowing their scope.
Finds reader Go readiness, unknown-as-empty inventories, missing no-pidfd member signaling, lost overlapping Stop replies and blocking lifecycle transport.
Requires authenticated noninheritable bootstrap, RAII resource ownership, complete behavioral backend tests and host-death fixtures that reject forced-cleanup false passes.
contracts: Historical verdict is accept_with_changes, explicitly not product-freeze approval.
No historical CI results were independently reproduced by the review; source assertions and runtime coverage are separate.
dependencies: public OS API references in the review
failures_or_limits: Named spike defects must not be relabeled as current baseline defects without present source comparison.
T4 could substitute forced kill, T6 could return NOTRUN, and selected output assertions allowed corruption/loss; this limits historical evidence.
gaps: Current closure of review requirements belongs to later implementation/test records, not this archival document alone.

evidence.quote: **Verdict:** `accept_with_changes` — The supervisor architecture is credible, and S5 contains meaningful assertions and controls. It does not establish every evidence claim or justify a product freeze: reader readiness, overlapping Stop requests, scan failures, pidfd absence, and T4 false passes need correction. Review was read-only and static; historical CI results were not independently reproduced.

| T3: one deadline, resistant tree cleanup, polite stop, and stop after root exit | yes | s5.rs:613–680 requires fixture readiness and three logged processes, independently checks survivors by PID and name, enforces wall time <=1500 ms, and distinguishes forced resistant cleanup from polite cleanup. The resistant tree must remain alive without stop; rootexit requires surviving descendants before stop and unchanged cached exit status afterward. These checks would fail for missing escalation, root-only termination, per-level grace accumulation, or premature Stopped. Scope is one small tree per request. |
| T4: each named host-death mode, bounded cleanup, and creation during host death | partly | s5.rs:684–757 checks six initial fixture processes, zero survivors by PID/name, and supervisor termination; the unsupervised orphan control is useful. However, if the host fails to exit within 15 seconds, the harness kills it and can still PASS. It does not assert the requested exit mechanism or status. Cleanup may take approximately 5.3 seconds before failing, rather than the reported ~1.3 seconds. Full-frame midspawn requires only the original six processes, so the additional spawn can be ignored without failing; neither creation nor its ordering after host death is asserted. |
| T5: isolation from SIGCHLD=SIG_IGN and a foreign reaper | partly | s5host.rs:192–250 creates the hostile conditions; s5.rs:817–848 asserts exits 42/7, forced tree cleanup, and an unrelated survivor. The host-child control must lose at least one status, which distinguishes the hostile host from the supervisor. It does not require all five losses or any positive reaped_by_foreign count, and it does not enforce a stop deadline. Coverage is the Rust host, as the result rows indicate. |
| T6: stale identity safety and retention while descendants live | partly | s5.rs:911–960 has a strong Unix recycled-group test: exact PID reuse, GONE acknowledgements, immediate Stop, a surviving sentinel, then a naive killpg control that kills it. However, recycling failures become non-failing NOTRUN. The live-descendant arm never calls Release and cannot validate 'Release notwithstanding'. Windows checks 150 distinct live sentinels while retaining the process handle, but its post-release test can PASS without observing reuse, and has no destructive comparison control. |
| T7: supervisor death, failed waits, platform cleanup, and restart | partly | s5.rs:1123–1171 requires two pending waits to fail with IO promptly and requires zero Windows survivors. Unix survivor counts are observations: the assertion accepts any outcome. Restart explicitly calls Sup::start again instead of exercising facade::sup's automatic replacement, so a broken lazy restart could pass. Pending spawn, stop, resize, and signal requests are not tested. |
| T8: PTY interaction, host state, close deadlines, and fast-exit output | partly | s5.rs:1175–1243 asserts prompt response, interrupt delivery, resize markers, stubborn-writer liveness/cleanup, and deadlines. Disabling TIOCSCTTY or retaining Windows' ignore flag provides useful interrupt controls; synchronous ClosePseudoConsole is a meaningful deadline control on pre-26100 Windows only. Unix host_sig_state checks five handlers/flags and merely counts blocked signals 1..31, omitting sigaction masks and full mask identity. The resize control checks absence of only one unexpected size. ptyloss_run checks only the PTYREPORT substring and ignores wait/EOF success; its macOS failure control is probabilistic. No test delays reader startup to expose the Go race. |
| T9: latency comparison and K4 | yes | s5.rs:1272–1375 implements rotated, same-job arms, 50 warm-ups, 500 measurements, and actual p50 <=1.25 assertions for the default and alternative paths. FAIL propagates to process exit and the workflow has no continue-on-error. This supports the reported benchmark methodology, not independent verification of the historical numbers. First-spawn timing is explicitly observational because its verdict is unconditional true. Only Rust, null stdio, and trivial pipe-mode programs are benchmarked; PTY and binding latency remain unmeasured. |
| T10: cross-host coverage | partly | T10 is the documented aggregation of T1/T3/T4, not a separate harness command. hosts_for selects Rust/Node/Python for T3/T4 and adds Bun/Deno for T1; the workflow supplies all five. This genuinely exercises the bindings, subject to those tests' weaknesses. It does not establish concurrent host-thread operation or extend T2/T5/T6/T7/T8/T9 to every runtime. |

| must_fix | PTY Go handshake and held-child cleanup | client.rs:465–467 releases the child before proving reader readiness. In addition, sup_unix.rs:698–724 leaves the Go pipe's write end inherited in the child until after its blocking read; closing the supervisor's write end therefore cannot produce the promised EOF. Existing tests do not cover host death before Go. | Implement explicit reader readiness before Go and test a deliberately delayed reader with complete output comparison. Verify whether readiness suffices under delayed draining; preserve the session leader through a drain acknowledgement or narrow the guarantee if necessary. Close unused Go/error-pipe ends in the child before waiting, and test cancellation, pre-Go host death, setup failure, and missing Go. |
| must_fix | Process inventory must distinguish unknown from empty | procs.rs returns empty inventories on enumeration failure and skips failed stat/getsid reads. sup_unix.rs:545–549 then interprets missing members as an empty session, reaps the pin, and declares gone. The harness shares these inventory helpers, so some observation failures can affect both implementation and oracle. alive also returns false for some EPERM-plus-stat-failure cases despite its conservative comment. | Return complete/partial/error inventory status and alive/dead/unknown liveness. Never reap or emit successful Stopped from an incomplete scan. Use dynamically sized macOS inventories, robust process identity checks, and independently validated test oracles. Inject enumeration, permission, parsing, and truncation failures while descendants remain alive. |
| must_fix | Kernels or policies without pidfd | sup_unix.rs:147 falls back for host monitoring, but signal_member:801–803 silently skips members whenever pidfd_open fails. Descendants in other groups survive on older kernels, under syscall filtering, or under descriptor exhaustion. The ADR's fallback description covers only host detection. [pidfd availability](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/pidfd_open.2.html). | Feature-detect host monitoring and member signalling separately. Either require and enforce supported pidfd syscalls or define a weaker fallback with explicit PID-reuse limitations; do not silently claim session cleanup. Test ENOSYS, EPERM, EMFILE, and pidfd_send_signal failure with a resistant descendant in a separate group. |
| must_fix | Full channels and backpressure | uds::send_all and Windows Sup::send perform blocking writes on the lifecycle owner. Unix exec_result also blocks that owner, and read_chan drains all decoded requests before returning to deadline work. Windows uses an unbounded internal event queue. A stalled reader, request flood, or stopped setup child can prevent host-death handling and escalation; the ConPTY close worker alone does not make deadlines independent. | Use nonblocking or asynchronous control transport with bounded queues, admission limits, reserved cleanup capacity, and fair processing budgets. Monitor exec-error pipes asynchronously and prioritize host death/deadlines. Define bounded completion or explicit failure for stalled supervisors. Test both channel directions full, partial frames, request floods, SIGSTOP, and children stalled before exec while another tree is stopping. |
| must_fix | Concurrent requests and host threads | sup_unix.rs:422–430 and sup_win.rs:342–349 retain only the first Stop request ID, leaving later callers blocked forever. Host write locks prevent frame interleaving but do not solve Stop/Release/Go races, startup failure races, or inherited mutex state after host fork. | Specify operation linearization and cancellation rules, preserve the earliest escalation deadline, and reply to every waiter. Make supervisor replacement and tree IDs generation-safe. Reject or reinitialize forked-host clients before acquiring inherited locks. Test simultaneous startup/spawn/stop/release, overlapping Stop deadlines, and supervisor death during those operations across real host threads. |

| must_fix | Channel authentication and inherited endpoints | The Unix channel authorizes whoever holds its host endpoint; CLOEXEC does not prevent fork-without-exec inheritance. Neither peer identity nor command authority is checked. Windows raw handle values in Spawn also require strict ownership validation. A startup token alone cannot distinguish a fork that inherited both endpoint and token. | Define the trust boundary explicitly. Bind bootstrap and command authorization to the original host using OS-authenticated identity where available, and prevent inherited clients from issuing commands or keeping authorization alive. Where the platform cannot enforce this, state the inherited-capability limitation. Validate all message states, descriptor counts, and transferred-handle ownership; test an inherited endpoint attempting Spawn/Stop/Release and malformed ancillary traffic. |
| must_fix | Windows supervisor-start inheritance race | client.rs:528–594 creates temporarily inheritable channel ends and a host process handle. HANDLE_LIST restricts this supervisor's inheritance but cannot prevent another host thread's unrestricted CreateProcess from inheriting them. A module-local mutex cannot coordinate unrelated native code. [Microsoft's explanation](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20200306-00/?p=103538). | Bootstrap without inheritable host handles, for example through a private authenticated rendezvous with bInheritHandles=FALSE and subsequent non-inheritable DuplicateHandle transfers. Arm host-death monitoring before accepting managed spawns. Test concurrent unrestricted process creation throughout startup, including startup failure and host death, and verify no unintended process retains channel endpoints or host handles. |
| must_fix | musl and libc compatibility | sup_unix.rs:1046–1100 unconditionally references nonstandard spawn actions for Linux. CI builds only the runner's GNU target; libc/API availability, static linking, old glibc compatibility, and child setup under musl are unproved. | Declare supported libc/version floors, gate optional spawn implementations by actual availability, and retain a tested fallback. Build and execute musl targets, including static configurations and oldest supported environments. Run lifecycle, descriptor isolation, PTY, failure, and latency tests on each creation backend before selecting it. |

| must_fix | T4 false passes and mid-spawn coverage | s5.rs:709–725 permits cleanup success after the harness substitutes a forced host kill for the requested death mode. Midspawn can pass with no additional tree created, and the claimed ~1.3-second bound is printed rather than enforced. | Require the host to exit through the requested mechanism; mark timeout as FAIL before cleanup. Measure cleanup from observed host death against an explicit bound. Add deterministic barriers around accepted Spawn, OS creation, registration, and Go, asserting expected extra creation for full frames and no creation for incomplete frames. Cover initial supervisor bootstrap separately. |
| must_fix | Release ownership and job-control coverage | The evidence attributes Release-independent pinning to T6, but that test never releases its live-descendant tree. No fixture changes process group, so session sweeping is untested and group-only implementations can pass T3/T4/T6. | Release a root-exited tree with resistant descendants in separate process groups, then kill the host and require complete cleanup. Add a group-only control that leaves those descendants alive, plus explicit zombie-pin observation. Require PID-reuse coverage on designated CI targets instead of silently accepting NOTRUN. |
| should_fix | Output, signal state, and restart assertions | T1 overstates its sampled signal checks; T2 does not compare complete output and accepts NOT_FOUND for a non-executable; T7 tests manual startup instead of automatic recovery. T8's marker-only fast-exit check and partial host-state snapshot leave failures undetected. | Compare exact expected pipe bytes and complete normalized PTY output; require successful wait and EOF. Use a minimal fixture that observes signal state before runtime changes and seed ignored/blocked signals in the host. Assert exact platform error classifications. Kill a facade-owned supervisor with pending operations and verify automatic restart through the same public API. |
| must_fix | Product output backpressure and resource bounds | Pump::start appends every byte to an unbounded Vec and treats all read errors as EOF. The spike's permanently draining threads avoid real consumer backpressure and can exhaust memory. Closing or slowing a product consumer also affects macOS loss guarantees and pre-26100 ConPTY shutdown. | Implement the product's bounded output policy, ordered loss/error reporting, cancellation, and continued draining during cleanup. Distinguish expected PTY EOF errors from real I/O failures. Test slow and abandoned consumers, output limits, and stubborn writers on both Windows build families. [ClosePseudoConsole requirements](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/console/closepseudoconsole). |
| must_fix | Creation-backend safety and PTY latency | T9 exercises alternatives only with trivial null-stdio children, so performance results do not establish equivalent behavior. CLONE_VM shares supervisor memory and CLONE_VFORK suspends its owner; a blocked setup child stalls all lifecycle work. The present Go hold disables that backend for PTYs, whose extra round trip is unmeasured. | Run the complete behavioral suite per backend and audit shared-memory child code, signal delivery, stack/TLS use, error paths, and blocked setup behavior. Keep Go-held PTYs off a suspending creation path unless the handshake is redesigned. Measure PID latency and spawn-to-exit separately for pipe and PTY modes; explicitly resolve K4 rather than treating an alternative benchmark as its fix. |
| should_fix | ADR acceptance and guarantee precision | The original Decision still permits reap-on-release, describes pipe containment by group, and retains an unmet K4 requirement. 'Everything else held' exceeds the tested scope. Ordinary setpgid within the existing session is covered by the intended session sweep and should not be described as an escape outside that session. | Integrate accepted refinements into the normative decision, identify observations and NOTRUN rows, and state session scanning and supervisor-death limits precisely. Keep product freeze conditional on the strengthened tests and an explicit performance decision. |
